statements.t: Executive Chair Greg Bentley said, “The progression throughout 2026 to date of BSY’s year-over-year ARR growth rate to 13%, exceeding our annual outlook range, reflects both the robustness of our focused end markets, and accounts’ confidence in our mutual trajectories for infrastructure AI.

At our Year in Infrastructure Awards last month, nearly 70% of our finalists leveraged AI in their projects, demonstrating how our software used at machine speed can significantly expand engineering capability to deliver better, more resilient infrastructure.”

CFO Werner Andre said, “Our strong Q3 results, expected continued momentum, and the programmatic acquisition of Eliis provide confidence in raising our constant currency ARR year‑over‑year growth range—excluding the impact from the Cohesive divestiture—to 12.5-13.5%.
The acquisition is expected to complement our Seequent subsurface portfolio.
Through our digital twin solutions, we help infrastructure professionals unlock the value of their data to transform project delivery and asset performance.

statements.t: Our results of operations have been, and in the future will be, affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates.

Because our prior period results include Cohesive and our results following October 13, 2026 will not, we expect year‑over‑year services revenues and cost of services expenses to decline through 2027, with a favorable impact on gross margin.
We expect the higher software subscription costs and reduced capitalization associated with the platforms to continue to affect general and administrative expenses.

We believe that we will continue to experience favorable growth in recurring revenues primarily due to our strong account retention and recurring revenues dollar‑based net retention rates, as well as the addition of new accounts with recurring revenues.

Related to our platform acquisitions, recurring revenues into new accounts will be captured as existing accounts starting with the second anniversary of the acquisition when such data conforms to the calculation methodology.

The timing, as well as the number and value of shares and/or outstanding convertible senior notes repurchased under the Repurchase Program, will be determined at our discretion and will depend on a variety of factors, including our assessment of the intrinsic value of our shares, the market price of our Class B common stock and outstanding convertible senior notes, general market and economic conditions,…
We will continue to evaluate whether share awards will be required to be received by awardees on a gross basis, or if net settlement may be elected by awardees.

While we intend to continue paying quarterly dividends, any future determination will be subject to the discretion of our Board of Directors and will be dependent on a number of factors, including our results of operations, capital requirements, restrictions under Delaware law, and overall financial condition, as well as any other factors our Board of Directors considers relevant.
